source_limitations: Official Oxford 3000 CEFR PDF directly inspected 2026-10-31 with page/line locators and four Oxford dictionary pages inspected. These word/POS observations and dictionary lexical sense leads are not independent exact-sense CEFR approval. Dictionary topic badges and Word of the Day footer are not exact-sense CEFR evidence. Self-authored Myanmar/example alternatives are unapproved; final dual-voice listening, physical iPhone and measured hosting remain unverified.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: The attitude or feeling expressed by someone's voice or words.
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: Her calm tone helped settle the argument.

records.editorial_risk: Voice attitude/quality (sense 1) must not be conflated with the general character of a document (sense 2), musical pitch or a colour shade.
records.independent_reviewer_task: Independent human editor must verify exact-sense CEFR, English definition, fluent Myanmar, original-example grammar, British pronunciation, source attribution and historical provenance; word/POS evidence and self-authored proposals are not approval.

dictionary_sense_lead.sense_summary: The first Oxford noun sense concerns the expressive quality of someone's voice; calm tone in the draft example belongs here, not the writing-atmosphere sense 2.

editorial_rewrite_candidate.original_example: Her reassuring tone helped the worried passengers feel calmer.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: In a way that must be true or must happen.
shortlist_snapshot.myanmar_meaning: မဖြစ်မနေ၊ သေချာပေါက်
shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: A higher price does not necessarily mean better quality.

records.editorial_risk: Draft affirmative definition says something must be true, while its example uses 'not necessarily' meaning not always or not definitely; review as distinct polarity-dependent construction.
records.independent_reviewer_task: Independent human editor must verify exact-sense CEFR, English definition, fluent Myanmar, original-example grammar, British pronunciation, source attribution and historical provenance; word/POS evidence and self-authored proposals are not approval.

dictionary_sense_lead.sense_summary: Oxford's not necessarily idiom indicates that a proposition is not always or definitely true, unlike affirmative necessarily indicating unavoidable truth; draft definition/example diverge.

editorial_rewrite_candidate.myanmar_meaning: မဖြစ်မနေ အဲဒီလို ဖြစ်သည်ဟု မဆိုလို (not necessarily)
editorial_rewrite_candidate.original_example: A higher price does not necessarily guarantee better quality.

dictionary_sense_lead.sense_summary: The second Oxford adjective sense is a sensible, workable idea or action; the shortlist's practical solution example fits this more specifically than the broad 'useful' definition.

shortlist_snapshot.english_definition: A particular skill or method used to achieve something.

shortlist_snapshot.example_sentence: The technician demonstrated a safer lifting technique.

records.editorial_risk: Oxford sense 1 is a countable method needing skill, whereas sense 2 is uncountable skill in execution; the example uses sense 1.
records.independent_reviewer_task: Independent human editor must verify exact-sense CEFR, English definition, fluent Myanmar, original-example grammar, British pronunciation, source attribution and historical provenance; word/POS evidence and self-authored proposals are not approval.

dictionary_sense_lead.sense_summary: The first Oxford noun sense is a countable learned method, while the second is the uncountable quality of skill; a safer lifting technique denotes the first sense.
